doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

title: Romy Britell asks whether gigging has lost its magic
summary: He says he loves playing more than ever and gets more from music now.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yes, Romy. RB: You’ve mentored so many people and you work so much, you know. And one time you told me, you said “I just want to play the piano.” Like, you know, you have to go to the gig, you have to make the money, but has it lost its magic? Playing a gig? Or do you just want to go home and not have to play for the people?

No not really. I mean honestly I would play anyway whether it was by myself or for people, it doesn’t matter. I’m not hung up on, oh geez there’s only a few people here, or the people aren’t paying attention. If they want to pay attention that might be to their advantage but if not I’m still enjoying it. I love playing more than ever. I guess that’s the thing. I get more out of music now than I ever have. So it’s been like a constant climb up, in terms of what I’m extracting from the music.
So I’m fortunate in that regard, and I do a lot of listening, just sitting and listening to music for long periods of time, and never tire of it.
